title: What does a negative exponent do to a power?
description: Ten to the power negative three and seven to the power negative two are written as fractions, and the video shows that one over ten to the power negative three is ten cubed. The rule for multiplying powers is then checked with a negative exponent. Keeko doubts whether the exponent is multiplied by the base.
teaching_notes: One idea: a negative exponent turns the power over, so it gives one over the power with the positive exponent. Watch for students who multiply the base by the negative exponent, or who think the answer must be a negative number.

source: Write 10 to the power −3 and 7 to the power −2 as fractions, show that 1 over 10 to the power −3 is 10³, and check the product rule with exponents 3 and −1.
video_script.why: A learner sees that a negative exponent means one over the power, and that the rule for multiplying powers still works with it.
video_script.substitution: the book's own ten to the power negative three, seven to the power negative two, and two cubed times two to the power negative one
video_script.anchor: ten to the power negative three and seven to the power negative two written on the board
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies the base seven by the exponent negative two
video_script.payoff_line: A negative exponent turns the power over into a fraction

final_answer.value: 1/1000 and 1/49; 1 over 10 to the power −3 is 10³; yes, the rules hold for integer exponents
final_answer.spoken: one over one thousand and one over forty nine; one over ten to the power negative three is ten cubed; yes, the rules hold for integer exponents

video_script.fraction_reading: 1/1000 is read one over one thousand, and 1/49 is read one over forty nine
video_script.design: One idea: a negative exponent turns the power over. Wrong idea: multiply the base by the exponent. The powers of ten are stepped down by dividing by ten each time, so the fraction form is seen before the rule is stated; the evaluated fractions only appear at the answer.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; 10^-3 and 7^-2 written on the board with question marks beside them

marks.two: 10^-3 and 7^-2 are written on the board
marks.ask: a question mark glows beside each power

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='two'/>We have ten to the power negative three, and seven to the power negative two.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How do we write each of them as a fraction?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: powers of ten stepping down: 10^2 = 100, 10^1 = 10, 10^0 = 1, then 10^-1 = 1/10, each step divided by 10

marks.down: 10^2 = 100, 10^1 = 10 and 10^0 = 1 are written in a column
marks.div: an arrow marked divide by 10 joins each step to the next
marks.next: the next step 10^-1 = 1/10 appears at the bottom

narration: <bookmark mark='down'/>Look at the powers of ten going down. Ten squared is a hundred, ten is ten, and ten to the power zero is one.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Each step down divides by ten.
<bookmark mark='next'/>The next step divides one by ten again, so it must be one tenth.

marks.given: 10^-3, 7^-2 and 2^3 x 2^-1 are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, ten to the power negative three, and seven to the power negative two. We also take two cubed times two to the power negative one.

beats.on_screen: To find: 10^-3 and 7^-2 as fractions; 1 over 10^-3; does the rule for multiplying powers hold?

marks.find: the words 10^-3 and 7^-2 as fractions are written
marks.rule: the words does the rule for multiplying powers hold are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write both powers as fractions.
<bookmark mark='rec'/>We show that one over ten to the power negative three is ten cubed.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>We also test the rule for multiplying powers.

marks.keep: the exponent 3 loses its minus sign and moves below the bar

narration: <bookmark mark='turn'/>Step one, take ten to the power negative three. A negative exponent turns the power over.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>It becomes one over ten to the power three, which is one over ten cubed.

marks.keep: the exponent 2 loses its minus sign and moves below the bar

narration: <bookmark mark='turn'/>Step two, do the same with seven to the power negative two.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>It becomes one over seven squared.

marks.frac: 1 / 10^-3 is written, and 10^-3 is replaced by 1/10^3
marks.flip: 1 divided by 1/10^3 is turned over into 10^3

narration: <bookmark mark='frac'/>Step three, take one over ten to the power negative three. From step one, that is one divided by one over ten cubed.
<bookmark mark='flip'/>Dividing by a fraction turns the fraction over.
<bookmark mark='cube'/>The result is ten cubed.

marks.rule: 2^3 x 2^-1 = 2^(3 + (-1)) = 2^2 is written from the rule
marks.same: 8 x 1/2 = 4 = 2^2 is written and the two results are joined

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step four, test the rule for multiplying powers of one base. The rule adds the exponents.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>Three plus negative one is two, so the result should be two squared. Check with numbers.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Two cubed is eight, and two to the power negative one is one half. Eight times one half is four, which is two squared.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 10^-3 = 1/1000, 7^-2 = 1/49; 1 / 10^-3 = 10^3; the rule holds for integer exponents

marks.pay: the turned over powers are boxed
marks.hold: the rule holds for integer exponents is written

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>A negative exponent turns the power over into a fraction.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Ten to the power negative three is one over one thousand. Seven to the power negative two is one over forty nine.
<bookmark mark='back'/>One over ten to the power negative three is ten cubed.
<bookmark mark='hold'/>Yes, the rule holds for integer exponents.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 7^-2 = 7 x (-2) = -14, struck out; 7^-2 = 1/7^2 beside it
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks seven to the power negative two is negative fourteen. Seven times negative two is negative fourteen.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But an exponent does not multiply the base. Seven to the power negative two is one over seven squared.
<bookmark mark='all'/>The minus sign only turns the power over.
